# Magic Portals parity — backlog

State at 2026-10-15, after wave 4d-1: the final comparison re-taken on the fixed build (first written 2026-09-15). What remains to make the **Supersonic port** (`game/` here since 2026-09-19; before, `Desktop/Supersonic-Engine/games/magicportals`)
match the original, in the order it should be done. Every spec named here lives under
`Magic-Portals-Enhanced/out/parity/specs/` (gitignored, local only — re-creatable from the reference library).

How to work on any item: `docs/parity.md` (rig, captures), `tools/parity/` (emu, capture_original, capture_screens,
markers, locate, compare, frames, port_build.bat). Port captures: Bash only, from this repository's root,
`build/game/MagicPortals.exe --level <name> --window 1280x720 --fixed-step --frames N --screenshot <absolute png>`.
Windows Smart App Control sometimes blocks a freshly linked exe ("Not Run" / "Permission denied" / "An Application Control
policy has blocked this file"): delete the exe and relink. Touching the source is not enough when the rebuild produces the
same bytes. **Every blocked launch shows Ivan a Windows notification: never loop relink/ctest retries** — run the
suites a change touches once each, and report what stayed blocked.

---

residuals not real; the second reading of chunk 8 (2-25 to 2-32), taken after the audit, found a medium the first reading missed on 5 of its 8 levels (CMP-14 on 2-26,
2-27, 2-30 and 2-31, the fireball on 2-28), and a chunk chosen because of the audit's miss makes that an upper bound; the other 15 chunks were not re-read and the audit's
sample holds no lightmapped chapter-2 level. So **61 / 65 / 2 are the rule's counts on the readers' verdicts and a lower bound on medium residuals**; the misses are
likely of two classes (lit-stone softness, a light effect on a moving object) on the chunks not re-read (R4d1-4). On the 21 levels no step touched, the two readings agree
on the verdict on 20 of 20 (the 21st, 2-32, is a fix seen at another tick), so the differences elsewhere are the build or a sharper look, not reader drift. (b) The
pairing is as wave 4b left it: the script-clock fit (four chapter 1-3 platform levels) and the two-clock reading were NOT re-run, h6.3 is not exactly f420, and a blink, a
pulse or a mover reads as a range (CMP-R1). (c) The independent verification (`R4d/verify1.json`: 10 gates, pass, 4 low) re-derived the counts and the matrix from the

No winning route has a stone begin near the threshold (at most 0.0), 3-12's kill is 71 % over, and the knights' crush (1.23) errs the same strict way, so no route is thin; **until this is settled a re-authored route should keep any stone's begin on the player under about 1.5** (the offset is at most 0.67, so that reads under 2.2 on the original). Next, before the route phase is called final or at latest before shipping: measure one stone landing on the player on the original (STK-1's capture) or settle it by arithmetic on the decoded gravity; if it holds, make the stone rows (the kill, the knights' crush, the shake, the hit sound) read the unbraked free flight (the peak velocity plus g dt along the line for each braked step between the peak and the begin), re-pin the falls of `AStoneThatBeginsToTouchThePlayerKillsHimAboveTwoAndAHalfAlone` and record it as a gameplay change of the watch (steps 142 and 152's reading).
      *Step 161's verifier checked it against all 86 routes: none is near the line, and the wave pushed with it open (R3c-1).*

- [x] **PORT2-2. The packager does not refuse a symbolic link to a sub-folder of a source tree, and a broken link is a traceback** (low-medium; tooling; `code`, Python only, no relink;
      GAMEPLAY: none). The brief says it "refuses a symlinked source"; it refuses a linked file and a linked tree root. With a tier folder such as `sprites/hd` replaced by a link,
      `content` exits 0 and builds a package without the files in it (35 instead of 37 in the unit tests' fixture; the 1x pictures are used silently, and `verify` passes because it
      uses the same model); a dangling link ends in an uncaught `FileNotFoundError` at `closure.py:88` (`os.path.getsize`). Cause: `Tree.__init__` records the link in `Tree.symlinks`,
      `os.walk` never descends it, and `is_symlinked` is asked only for files already in the plan. Reproduction: `out/parity/program/PORT/PORT2/verify1/d2.py` and `d2.txt` (verifier D1,
      reviewer D2). Fix: in `plan_content` raise `PackageError` if any tree it reads has an entry in `Tree.symlinks` other than the root, guard the `getsize`, add two unit tests (a
      linked sub-folder, a broken link: 35 -> 37). A link is not something the converter or the extraction makes, and the sweep from the package alone would show the loss; `tools/package/README.md`
      and `docs/packaging.md` say what is and is not refused. Next: the next change to the packager; it changes the md5s of `closure.py` and `test_package.py` and nothing the game reads.
      **[Annotated 2026-10-26, DEVLOG Session 67, planning step 208 (PORT-10): CLOSED. `closure.py` measures a link with `lstat` (a broken link no longer ends in a traceback) and `package.py` refuses a symbolic link ANYWHERE in a tree it reads, at its own name (`original:sprites/hd is a symbolic link ...`), before it plans: a linked sub-folder, a broken link, a link nothing names. Three tests in `test_package.py` (a linked sub-folder, a broken link, a broken link inside a package that `verify` reports) ran on Windows (symbolic links are allowed on this PC) and in WSL; where a system will not make a link they skip AND print the reason.]**

      differ by the same amount between platforms. Whether it ever matters is for a listener. The engine's way out, if it does, is to decode a game's own clips and hand them over with

- [ ] **PORT12-3. The licence is a proposal** (medium; release; `owner-call`; GAMEPLAY: none). `LICENSE` is the MIT No Attribution text, the same as the engine's, with the engine's holder and year. It was chosen because the engine this game is built on is under it, so the two files need no reconciling and the licence asks nothing of a player or of a later maintainer (no notice has to travel with it). The alternatives, in one paragraph: the MIT licence (the same, with a notice that must be kept), the Apache License 2.0 (a patent grant and a notice file), or a copyleft licence (the GPL family: a change by anyone must be shared in kind; the engine's own licence would not stop that, but the libraries in `NOTICE.md` are all permissive). The owner confirms or replaces it before the repository is public.

- [ ] **PORT12-9. `tools/ci/test_check_public.py` leaves its synthetic repositories in the temporary folder on Windows** (low; tests; `known`; found by the close of step 210, which counted them; GAMEPLAY: none). Every test that makes a repository (`SyntheticRepos.make`, the folder test at line 179 and the clone test at line 836) creates a folder with the prefix `check_public_test_` and removes it in `cleanup()` with `shutil.rmtree(folder, ignore_errors=True)`. Git writes its loose objects read-only, Windows will not delete a read-only file, and `ignore_errors=True` hides the refusal, so each folder stays: **17,175 had gathered in `%TEMP%` on this PC between 15:38 and 23:10 on 2026-10-27**, from the runs of the roles of the step (a sample folder held 21 read-only files, 2,026 bytes). No test failed and no gate saw it; the Linux subsystem, where the removal works, left none (0 in its `/tmp`). The close deleted them by the exact prefix, together with the step's own scratch (two `mut-p12-*` mutation copies of 63 MB each, two `mp-make-app-*` folders and the reviewer's and the committer's scratch folders), and left every folder it could not attribute to this step (among them 14 empty `mp-world-test-*` folders dated 12:06 to 12:09 on 2026-10-27, before this step began). The fix is small and is not made here, because the close commits no code and the gates measured the committed bytes: give `cleanup()` an error handler that clears the read-only flag and retries (`shutil.rmtree(folder, onexc=...)`, or `onerror=` before Python 3.12), and a check that a run leaves no folder with that prefix in `tempfile.gettempdir()`. Until then, delete the folders after a run of this module on Windows. `tools/apple/test_make_app.py` (prefix `mp-make-app-`) left two small folders too; that was not looked into.

## 7. The beta tester's reports of 2026-11-07 (steps 224 to 227)

Four reports (the owner's, relayed with a tester's): a black strip in the sky on a 2340 x 1080 phone, "the gas canisters don't explode", "the stone ball hits that rotating floor, and it glitches", and the launcher icon's white bars. Fixed or answered in the tree and **not released** (0.1.6 awaits the owner's word). What stays open:

- [ ] **SKY-1. The wide-window sky is grown, which crops its height (18 percent at 2340 x 1080, 24 at 21:9), and nobody has looked at a frame** (low; design call; `owner-call`; GAMEPLAY: none). Step 224. The alternative is Step 212's `side_fill` way (extend the picture's edge, feather it): no crop, a seam. The switch is `game/data/sky.json` `static_sky.wide_view.enabled`. A capture at 2340 x 1080 (`build/game/MagicPortals.exe --level level2 --window 2340x1080 --fixed-step --frames N --screenshot <absolute png>`, Bash only) before and after is the thing to look at.
- [ ] **SKY-2. The 1.0 u tolerance leaves up to 0.5 u (1 to 2 pixels) bare per side for a window between aspect 1.779 and 1.78125 (1282 x 720, 1366 x 767), and the scale steps from 1.0 to 1.0044 at 456 u** (low). Step 224. A tolerance of 0.25 (side_fill's `min_gap_units`) caps it at 0.125 u and would start to grow 1366 x 768 by 0.3 percent. Also latent: a sky with a `scroll` would not stay seamless under the growth (no level has one).
- [ ] **ICON-1. No `<monochrome>` layer, and what Android 16 and 17's Pixel launcher does with an icon that has none is not known; the icon was seen only in the API 33 emulator's launcher (a circle mask), never on the owner's phone** (low; `owner-call`; GAMEPLAY: none). Step 225. Ask whether Themed icons is on; a monochrome layer would be the gear and ball as one colour (`<monochrome android:drawable=...>`, a fifth and sixth file per density) and needs a segmentation of the original's tile that the foreground (an opaque square) does not give.
- [ ] **HINGE-1. 2-31 after the stone has landed on the plank is finished by two unusual plays only (a portal swap with the stone, 9 shots; or an aim through a window of about 1 u in y, 7 shots), and no committed test covers the stone drop** (medium; `owner-call`; GAMEPLAY: 2-31). Step 226. Whether a human gets through is a hand-play question; whether the ORIGINAL's 2-31 behaves like this (the plank at its stop, the stone resting on the anchor) is inferred from Box2D's source, no clip shows it. The two routes are in `out/parity/tester_2026-11-07/`; installing either moves `tests/golden/controls_census.json`'s `shot_taps` (688) and the lists are the owner's to sign (Step 220's rule).
- [ ] **HINGE-2. The engine's `solveSpring` measures from the spring's rest angle on the plain atan2 reading, so a spring whose rest angle is near pi still wraps** (low; engine; GAMEPLAY: none; no game here uses a spring). Step 226, `ARCHITECTURE.md` says so. Fix in the engine's repository when something needs it.
- [ ] **HINGE-3. 2-30's and 3-15's windows are [0, 3.1416], 7e-6 past pi: the unwrap now applies to them, and their counter-clockwise stop is out of reach of the level's own geometry (floors cap the plank's tilt near 13 to 15 degrees)** (low; GAMEPLAY: none found). Step 226. Only a tunnelled state could reach the stop; the original's behaviour there is unmeasured.
- [ ] **GAS-1. Ask the tester what he meant, and let him replay 2-15 and 2-23 on 0.1.6** (low; `owner-call`). Step 227: his video shows every barrel he touched blowing and every statue left standing (0.1.5's behaviour); Step 223 frees them. Separately, 2-23's left barrel blown on its crate (before the crate burns) does not take the left statue although it rests 79.0 u from the statue's collider top against a grab of 80: the cause (the crate on the ray, or the one-unit reach margin) was not isolated, and the original is not measured.
- [ ] **SKY-3. 1-03 shows a black column 209 pixels wide at the left edge of its first screen on a 2340 x 1080 screen, and nine levels with no sky of their own show dark side columns** (low; found by the 0.1.6 audit's first look at wide frames; GAMEPLAY: none). Step 228. 1-03 (`level2`): the picture is byte-identical in 0.1.5, in 0.1.6 and with `wide_view` off, and the column is exactly the 49.8 u a wide view adds beyond 16:9; INFERENCE: level art drawn unlit (`arch.ent` reaches 128 u left of the scene's edge), `level2.tscn` has no black node. The nine (1-28, 3-10, 3-14, 3-17, 3-20, 3-26, 4-23, 4-24, 4-26) have dark columns where the level's own background ends (3-17 seen: about 21 u a side). Not shown to be what the tester saw (his came and went with walking). A look at the unlit art, or a sky that is allowed to show beyond a level's edge, is the next step; a frame at 2340 x 1080 of each is the evidence.
- [ ] **CLIP-1. The engine's capsule-against-hull contact still has no direction when a capsule's axis runs through a hull's surface (`CollisionHull.cpp` :476 and :481 answer the world's UP), and the port keeps only a PORTAL ARRIVAL out of it** (medium; engine; GAMEPLAY: none found). Step 229. Anything else that could put the player's axis through an underside - a lift or a door closing on him, an upward exit velocity into a hull over the exit, a body that pushes him into one - still gets sent UP into the platform; none of the 128 routes does (the routes suite is identical to the tick with and without the fix, in all four modes), and none was tried. The fix is the engine's: the exit (or nearest) face's outward normal in place of (0,1,0) where its dot with up is negative, then the pin bump and the 128 routes again; it would move every chamfer landing (a chamfer's normal is not exactly up), so it wants its own measurement. Until then `Portals.cpp`'s `LowerOutOfOverhead` is the only guard.
- [ ] **CLIP-2. That the original never clips under a ceiling is INFERRED from Box2D's polygon-circle contact, not measured, and the port lowers the arrival at once (9.5 u at most) where the original would ease him out; the tester's exact taps were not reproduced** (low; `owner-call`; GAMEPLAY: the player's arrival under a platform). Step 229. If a clip of the original with a portal opened close under a ceiling can be had (1-21 under the slab by the plate, 1-20 under the plank), compare the first ticks after the arrival with the port's. The end state of the old code (centre (314.10, 142.22)) matches the owner's picture to 1 or 2 units; the taps that led to it are not known. The 0.5 u margin under the face (`kAxisClearancePx`) is judged a numerical tolerance and is a constant, not a table row (architecture rule 1): if the owner would have it as data, it is one key in `game/data/transit.json`, `Transit` and `LoadTransit`, and the inline transit JSON of `test_mp_portal`.

Walking off the left end of 2-17's right-hand ledge (`platform_no_emissive_ent_1146`) burns the player in the air, and whether the ORIGINAL lets him survive that drop is not measured; only the owner can overrule the air-brake ruling that causes it** (medium; `owner-call`; GAMEPLAY: the air brake, Step 213's ruling). Step 230. The owner reported (2026-11-08) that he cannot get 2-17's gold because he dies jumping down from "the right platform at the bottom", and that "in the original it was possible". On the port the fire agent (reach 32, centre to centre) kills him in the AIR, on tick 476 at 19.0 from the flame, after a walk of 9 or more ticks off 1146's left end (walks of 7 and 8 ticks burn too, at 30.9 and 26.2): the walk pad is ignored in the air and Step 213's ruling (`data/player.json` `movement.air_decay_rate_hz` 120, a share of 1) keeps all his x velocity; neither the port nor the original's script has a fall rule. Step 230 gave the route a gold that does NOT use the drop (8 portals, 5 of 5 crystals, medal 3, tick 506); that does NOT make the drop survivable, and his own drop still burns on the port. Lowering `air_decay_rate_hz` is the only global lever (45 gives a share of 0.645) and it takes 1-04's gold and 2-30's leap out of reach again and re-breaks the 20 routes Step 213 re-timed: they need 1.0 and this drop needs well under 0.8 by the model, so no single share serves both, and a per-level override would be invented behaviour. UNMEASURED: the original's share is `min(1, fps / 60 x 0.86)`; the model has the three walk-offs survive at the rig's 26 frames a second (0.373), leaves 60 (0.86) undecided, and burns him from about 70 (1.0) as on the port; it leaves out the original's two-frame-late ground flag and its frame-time-scaled walk step, which push a held walk-off the wrong way. ASK: which platform, held or tapped, on which phone and at what frame rate. WHAT SETTLES IT: a rig clip of the original doing the walk-off from 1146's left end, held and tapped, with its frame rate stated (`docs/parity.md` sections 1 and 2). If the owner overrules the ruling, check `test_mp_routes` (all 128), `--display 30,60,90,120,144`, `--controls modern`, `test_mp_census`, `test_mp_player`, `test_mp_timebase`, `test_mp_demolish` and `test_mp_layer`.

The carried key's -45 degree tilt (fixKeyAngle) is not built, so the key's flight into its keyhole turns it from upright to -90 over the first 666 ms where the original's turns it from about -45; and the flight was checked against F9's numbers and the pictures' orientation, not against a capture of the port** (low; `owner-call`; GAMEPLAY: none, the key's look only). Step 233 (PORT-29). The original rewrites a carried key's angle every frame (`fixKeyAngle`, bytes 442683..443218, called at #1132 of `ETHCallback_key`; its `pickedAngle` is -45; footage F9 #203-#205 shows the key tilted at the player's back) and w0 of its fly-in takes `GetAngle()` of that; the port draws a carried key upright (0), so w0's angle is 0 and the first leg turns it the whole 90. Building it changes the look of EVERY carried key, a part of it (the interpolation from the angle at the pick, and the side it settles on) is inferred, and nobody has seen the port's flight on a screen: a capture of 3-08 or 3-18 at the unlock (`MagicPortals.exe --level level7b --place ...`, `main.cpp` capture-only warp) beside F9's #206-#224 is the evidence, and then the tilt. The flight's start angle is the picture's own, `-sprite.rotation` of the key node (0: none of the 81 `key*` nodes of `out/levels` carries a rotation), passed in at the one call that draws it (`syncSprites`' key branch, and 0 in `effectOwnerPoint` and `updateEffects` for a boss's dropped key), so that the tilt is one number to add.

A knight braked with something in sight is drawn standing, where the original draws the last frame its stride wrote, and the owner's 3-05 report ("the right enemy sometimes gets stuck in front of the door, in the walking animation") is not known to be this** (low; `owner-call`; GAMEPLAY: none, the picture only). Step 234 (PORT-30). `game/data/art.json` `minion.watch_stands` is true: `false` restores the decode (ETHCallback_minion #1183-1205 sets the standing frame only `if (entityInSight == null)`, so a braked knight with something in sight keeps its stride's frame, mid-step in 3 of 4 columns). The port's static walk has no stall (a 2000-tick probe), and the two reproductions of Step 234 do not settle what the owner saw: on 3-05 with the player put on the lift door's button the right knight freezes 291 ticks (4.9 s) where it saw him and 126 ticks (2.1 s) against the door, mid-stride under the decode, but the player is shot dead within 129 ticks of stepping on the button, and a player walking toward the knight dies before it can block him (so "H1", the player's body in its first leg with `holdMs` 0, is neither shown nor excluded). If the owner says the legs kept cycling, this change does nothing for his report. Footage of the original at a sighting (`docs/parity.md` sections 1-2) settles whether its knight stands or freezes. `test_mp_routes --only <route> --trace N` now prints a second line per minion (arm, vx, seeing, spotted, dest, hold, elapsed), so the next report can be told from the numbers.
